newsitem.title: USA: Debt service climbing for Wis. road bonds -- report.
newsitem.headline: Debt service climbing for Wis. road bonds -- report.

text.p: - Wisconsin debt service payments on bonds sold to fund major transportation projects over the years will exceed the amount of proceeds from future debt issuance, the Legislative Audit Bureau warned.

The report, released this week, said there were $1.7 billion of highway rehabilitation needs, plus another $1.2 billion of identified expansion projects through fiscal 2009. Meanwhile, state support for local road projects was continuing to grow, according to the report.

"By 2001-02, if we keep bonding at the current rate, we'll be paying more out in debt service than we realize from the sale of bonds," warned Judith Frye, Wisconsin's assistant state auditor. "We expect this to be an important issue for the next legislative session," Frye said.

In addition, light-rail projects that might require state funding assistance are being explored in Milwaukee and Madison, the report said. In Milwaukee alone a light-rail project is estimated to cost nearly $780 million.

The report said that the growth in vehicle registration fee and motor fuel tax revenues may not keep up with inflation and could cause a shortfall in overall transportation funding levels in the coming biennium.
In the report, released this week, the bureau indicated that 68 percent of transportation capital projects were to be funded with revenue bonds backed by vehicle registration fee revenues.
In 1997, an estimated 28.4 cents of each dollar of those fees will be dedicated to debt service, compared to 6.5 cents in 1984, the report said.

The report outlined several options to increase revenues, such as hiking vehicle registration fees, increasing gas taxes and giving local governments the ability to raise their own revenues for transportation projects through local gas taxes and registration fees.
